key_insight: The paper combines local reachability geometry with reinforcement learning so a policy selects intermediate waypoints for multi-impulse interplanetary transfers, while classical Lambert and terminal reconstructions turn that choice into a feasible trajectory.
engineering_relevance: This provides a reusable trajectory-design interface that improves policy reuse across different departure states and supports near-reference maneuver quality for Earth-Mars transfer planning.
method: Build a local first-order reachability map that converts bounded velocity perturbations into an ellipsoidal set of candidate next-node positions.
Use reinforcement learning to choose a waypoint inside that reachable set, then apply Lambert reconstruction to generate the ballistic transfer arc.
Finish with a terminal two-impulse reconstruction and a linear maneuver-demand reward signal to guide learning.
evidence_signal: On a two-body Earth-Mars benchmark, three independent runs achieved a mean cost of 10.23 km/s, only 1.72% above the local sequential convex programming reference, and the multi-state policies completed all 10,000 held-out departures without impulse-cap violations.
watch_item: The approach depends on local first-order reachability and two-body benchmark assumptions, so performance may degrade when higher-fidelity dynamics, constraints, or larger model mismatch are introduced.
paper_title: Reachability-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Impulse Interplanetary Transfers
